claims.claim: For pairwise MUBs, their centered rank-one projectors span mutually orthogonal five-dimensional traceless diagonal subspaces; seven MUBs are equivalent to an orthogonal decomposition of the 35-dimensional traceless Hermitian space into seven such subspaces.
claims.evidence: For Q_ki=P_ki−I/6, direct calculation gives Tr(Q_ki Q_kj)=δ_ij−1/6 and, between distinct MUBs, Tr(Q_ki Q_lj)=0. The within-basis Gram matrix I−J/6 has rank five and its span is exactly the traceless diagonal space. Seven mutually orthogonal such spans have dimension 7·5=35; conversely their orthogonality gives Tr(P_kiP_lj)=1/6 and hence the MUB condition.
claims.search_method: Direct Hilbert–Schmidt calculation and dimension count.

claims.claim: Given any six MUBs in C^6, let W be the orthogonal complement of their six centered diagonal subspaces. They extend to a seventh MUB if and only if every pair of matrices in W commutes; if so, the extension is unique.
claims.evidence: The six orthogonal subspaces have dimension 30, so dim W=5. Any extension has its five-dimensional traceless diagonal space equal to W. Conversely, commuting Hermitian matrices in W are simultaneously diagonalizable; dimension five makes W the entire traceless diagonal space in that eigenbasis. Orthogonality then gives overlap squared 1/6 with every original basis ray. The resulting full diagonal algebra has unique rank-one minimal projections, establishing uniqueness up to phases and permutation.
claims.search_method: Dimension count, simultaneous diagonalization, and uniqueness of minimal projections in a maximal diagonal algebra.

claims.claim: A complete set of seven MUBs satisfies the reconstruction identity Σ_ki Tr(AP_ki)P_ki=A+Tr(A)I and the tensor identity Σ_ki P_ki⊗P_ki=I+F.
claims.evidence: Each centered simplex has frame operator equal to the identity on its five-dimensional span. The seven orthogonal spans therefore reconstruct every traceless Hermitian matrix; complex-linear extension and Σ_ki P_ki=7I yield the stated formula for every matrix A. Pairing the formula with B gives ΣTr(AP)Tr(BP)=Tr(AB)+Tr(A)Tr(B), which is the nondegenerate product-matrix pairing with I+F and proves the tensor identity.
claims.search_method: Simplex-frame reconstruction followed by the nondegenerate trace pairing on tensor products.

claims.claim: In a complete set, every unit vector x obeys Σ_ki |⟨x,v_ki⟩|^4=2; a vector unbiased to any chosen six bases must be a ray of the remaining basis.
claims.evidence: Applying claim 2 to P_x and pairing with P_x gives the fourth-moment sum 2. Six unbiased bases contribute 36·(1/6)^2=1. The remaining probabilities satisfy Σp_i=Σp_i^2=1; since p_i≥0, Σp_i(1−p_i)=0 forces one p_i=1 and all others zero, so x is a remaining-basis ray.
claims.search_method: Substitution into the reconstruction identity and an exact probability-simplex argument.

claims.claim: For any hypothetical complete set and any fixed identification C^6=C^2⊗C^3, the sum of the 42 qubit reduced purities is exactly 30.
claims.evidence: The swap trick gives Tr[(Tr_B P)^2]=Tr[P⊗P(F_A⊗I_BB)]. Summing claim 2's tensor identity produces Tr[(I+F_A⊗F_B)(F_A⊗I)]=Tr(F_A)Tr(I_BB)+Tr(I_AA)Tr(F_B)=2·9+4·3=30.

claims.claim: Relative to any fixed C^2⊗C^3 factorization, a complete set contains at most 18 product rays and at most three entirely product bases. Equality forces every other ray to be maximally entangled.
claims.evidence: Every qubit marginal of a pure 2×3 state has purity at least 1/2; product rays have purity 1, and purity 1/2 is exactly maximal entanglement. If P rays are product, claim 4 gives 30≥P+(42−P)/2, hence P≤18. Three product bases use all 18 allowed product rays, and equality in the summed lower bound forces every other purity to be 1/2.
claims.search_method: Sharp reduced-purity bounds combined with the exact total-purity identity.

claims.claim: For any fixed conjugation K, a complete set has at most 12 K-real rays and hence at most two bases consisting entirely of K-real rays.
claims.evidence: Choose a K-real orthonormal coordinate basis and Ω=Σe_r⊗e_r. For a ray v, ⟨Ω|P_v⊗P_v|Ω⟩=|Σv_r^2|^2 lies in [0,1] and equals one exactly when the ray is K-real. Claim 2 gives total statistic ⟨Ω|(I+F)|Ω⟩=12, so at most 12 terms can equal one; six rays per real basis then gives at most two such bases.
claims.search_method: Tensor-moment evaluation against the conjugation-associated maximally correlated vector.

claims.claim: Two direct tensor-product bases in C^2⊗C^3 are mutually unbiased if and only if their respective qubit bases and qutrit bases are mutually unbiased.
claims.evidence: Product overlaps factor as α_rsβ_tu. If every product is 1/6, fixing t,u makes all α_rs equal; row normalization in dimension two forces α_rs=1/2, after which β_tu=1/3. Conversely, multiplying local squared overlaps 1/2 and 1/3 gives 1/6.
claims.search_method: Exact factorization of product-state overlaps and local row normalization.

claims.claim: Every triple of MUBs in C^3 extends uniquely to four MUBs, and the rays unbiased to all three are exactly the fourth basis.
claims.evidence: Every 3×3 complex Hadamard matrix is equivalent to the Fourier matrix. After fixing the standard/Fourier pair, the cyclic-autocorrelation equation restricts a common-unbiased ray to x_pq with six exact pairs. Integer Eisenstein enumeration found precisely (0,1),(0,2),(1,0),(1,1),(2,0),(2,2), precisely the two asserted orthogonal triples, and squared raw overlap three between the triples. Choosing either triple as the third basis leaves exactly the other as the common-unbiased locus and unique completion.
claims.search_method: Hadamard dephasing plus exhaustive exact enumeration in Z[ω] over all p,q in Z_3.

claims.claim: If three unit qubit rays form a tight frame with frame operator 3I/2 and are all unbiased to one qubit basis, that basis is the unique qubit basis unbiased to all three rays.
claims.evidence: Their centered projectors lie in the two-dimensional zero-diagonal plane associated with the given basis and sum to zero. They cannot span only one line: equal norms would make them three signed copies of one vector, whose odd signed sum cannot vanish. Thus they span the plane, and any basis unbiased to all three must have its diagonal Bloch axis in the unique orthogonal line, which determines the original unordered basis.

claims.claim: No maximally entangled vector in C^2⊗C^3 is unbiased to three pairwise MUB direct tensor-product bases.
claims.evidence: For such a vector, ρ_B=Π_S/2. Uniformity over each product basis implies ⟨b|Π_S|b⟩=2/3, so the ray S-perp is unbiased to all three local qutrit bases and is a ray of their unique fourth basis. Using the other two fourth-basis rays as Schmidt vectors, every normalized conditional qubit ray is unbiased to the same Schmidt basis. For each local qutrit basis the three conditional rays have frame operator 3I/2 and are also unbiased to its associated qubit basis. Claim 9 therefore makes all three qubit bases identical, contradicting their pairwise mutual unbiasedness.
claims.search_method: Exact marginal and conditional-state reduction using claims 7–9.

claims.claim: A complete seven-MUB set in C^2⊗C^3 cannot contain three direct tensor-product bases; consequently it contains at most two such bases.
claims.evidence: Three direct-product bases contribute 18 product rays. Claim 5 then forces all 24 rays in the other four bases to be maximally entangled. Every one would nevertheless have to be unbiased to the three direct-product bases, contradicting claim 10.
claims.search_method: Contradiction combining the sharp purity budget with the maximally-entangled-vector obstruction.

claims.claim: If one basis is standard and every vector in every other basis has coordinates consisting entirely of fourth roots, or entirely of sixth roots, divided by √6, then the MUB family has at most two bases.
claims.evidence: The argument rigorously proves two globally uniform cases: two fourth-root-flat vectors would require A^2+B^2=6, impossible modulo 3, while two sixth-root-flat vectors would require A^2+AB+B^2=6, impossible modulo 2. The checker exhaustively confirmed all 4^6 and 6^6 sums. But the claim's literal quantifier placement also permits different vectors or bases to choose different alphabets. Such cross-overlaps are sums of twelfth roots and neither congruence applies. The exact witness below even shows a mixed fourth/sixth pair can have the required overlap. No proof or exhaustive classification of mixed families is supplied, so the bound at that broader stated scope remains unresolved.
claims.search_method: Exhaustive Gaussian/Eisenstein-integer enumeration for the uniform cases and an exact Q(ζ_12) scope check for the omitted mixed case.
claims.witness: Let ξ=exp(πi/6). The unit vectors d=(ξ^0,ξ^6,ξ^3,ξ^9,ξ^9,ξ^3)/√6 and s=(ξ^0,ξ^8,ξ^8,ξ^4,ξ^0,ξ^4)/√6 are respectively fourth-root-flat and sixth-root-flat, and the persisted checker proves the raw inner-product squared modulus is 6, hence |⟨d,s⟩|^2=1/6.

claims.claim: For the standard dimension-six Weyl construction, order-six isotropic subgroups L≤Z_6^2 give stabilizer bases, and two such bases are mutually unbiased exactly when their label subgroups intersect only at zero.
claims.evidence: The 36 Weyl operators are Hilbert–Schmidt orthogonal. An isotropic order-six label subgroup spans a six-dimensional unital commutative star-algebra in M_6; faithfulness and dimension force six one-dimensional joint eigenspaces, hence a stabilizer basis. Its traceless diagonal algebra is exactly the span of its five nonidentity labels. Two such spaces are orthogonal exactly when those label sets are disjoint, equivalently L∩M={0}, and centered-diagonal orthogonality is exactly mutual unbiasedness. The checker also verified L=L-perp for every enumerated order-six isotropic subgroup.
claims.search_method: Weyl commutator and trace calculation, supplemented by exhaustive exact subgroup enumeration.

claims.claim: At most three pairwise MUB stabilizer bases arise from the dimension-six Weyl construction, and three are attainable.
claims.evidence: Every subgroup of order six contains nonzero 2-torsion. Z_6^2 has exactly the three nonzero involutions (3,0),(0,3),(3,3), and pairwise trivially intersecting subgroups must contain distinct ones, giving the upper bound three. The horizontal, vertical, and diagonal cyclic subgroups attain it. Exhaustive enumeration found 12 order-six isotropic subgroups, 24 disjoint triples, and no disjoint quadruple.
claims.search_method: Involution counting plus exhaustive generation and exact intersection testing of all subgroups of Z_6^2.

target_evidence: The exact target asks for either an unrestricted nonexistence proof for seven MUBs in C^6 or an exact construction of seven bases. The draft explicitly says the unrestricted case remains open and supplies neither alternative, so it does not fully resolve the target. Claims 0–11 and 13–14 nevertheless establish substantive structural identities, uniqueness reductions, entanglement restrictions, a direct-product obstruction, and a sharp Weyl-stabilizer bound; these constitute valid partial progress despite claim 12's unresolved mixed-alphabet scope. The final writeup does not claim a full solution, and claimed_resolution is PARTIAL, so that claimed resolution is accurate.
